title: Clone Intake, Quarantine, and Testing
objective: Control incoming clone risk through identity checks, quarantine, representative testing, and documented release.

terms.definition: The controlled receipt, identification, documentation, inspection, and routing of incoming plant material.
Physical and workflow separation of material with unresolved health or identity status from released stock.
A traceable record of who collected, transferred, stored, or handled a sample from collection through testing and decision.
A sample selected by a defined plan so the tested material reasonably addresses the population, tissue, organism, and decision of interest.
A defined set of assays or target organisms included in a testing program; a panel only supports conclusions about its stated targets and methods.
A documented decision that material may leave quarantine or another controlled status under the program's stated criteria.
A negative test result obtained when the target is actually present, potentially because of assay performance, sampling, timing, tissue choice, or target distribution.

coreScience: Incoming clones can introduce pests, pathogens, viroids, mislabeled genetics, resistant organisms, and unknown chemical residues. Quarantine separates this uncertainty from established mother and production stock.

Testing answers a defined question about the submitted tissue and method. A negative result does not prove permanent freedom from every organism. Uneven pathogen distribution, tissue choice, timing, and sampling design can contribute to false-negative results, so organism-specific laboratory instructions must control sampling.
Identity and health are separate release gates. A clone may match the expected cultivar yet fail health criteria, or test negative for a limited pathogen panel while its identity remains uncertain.
cultivationRelevance: Assign an intake ID before unpacking. Record source and transport conditions, photograph condition, inspect under magnification, isolate material, use dedicated tools, and release only through a documented decision.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Supplier and provenance; clone count and IDs; arrival condition; quarantine location; pest observations; sample chain of custody; laboratory and method; results; retest; release/reject/destruction decision.

For clone intake, quarantine, and testing, record the relevant developmental stage, environment, operator or treatment condition, and time sequence so the biological response can be separated from handling and facility effects.

Record the defined success endpoint, failures and off-types, replicate or batch variation, and any identity, health, rooting, survival, or follow-up test used to verify that the apparent result persisted after establishment.

misconceptions: A supplier certificate replaces quarantine. Visible similarity alone does not prove equivalent physiological state, health status, or later performance; identity and outcome measurements answer different questions.

Testing one leaf certifies an entire shipment. A single observation or negative symptom check cannot exclude latent infection, developmental history, or protocol-specific effects; use the appropriate follow-up test or repeated observation.
Quarantine ends when plants look normal. Cultivar names, appearance, and one successful batch are not substitutes for traceable identity, controlled comparison, and repeatable propagation outcomes.
evidenceLimits: Required panels, quarantine duration, destruction, reporting, and sample instructions are jurisdiction-, laboratory-, organism-, and facility-specific and require release-time review. This lesson does not prescribe a universal pathogen panel or quarantine period.
